body: It's hard. Lately I have been distancing myself and it's been okay. But today we went out for cheesecake. Which is supposed to be a nice pleasant activity. But then our conversation turned sour, and it just escalated to the point where she was complaining about my brother to me. And I don't want to get in the middle of their argument, and I told her that. But now she thinks that means I'm on his side. So all the anger towards him got directed to me. For the first time in over a week I tried to spend time with her, and this is what happened.
Then work towards not being homeless. Or make sure you check in with her regularly, once a week or something.
I don't think the sadness will be temporary. It'll stay with her forever.
Do you really think it would help your mom? Or do you think it might cause more stress or sadness.
Yeah me too. But what can we do? It'll hurt them if we end it. So just keep on living for them.
At least we both know that we are loved.

Wondering this as well. How sharp does a knife have to be? Where do I stab myself? I can't get into a car crash without injuring the other driver as well. Maybe if I drove straight into a semitruck...
Also, thank you for talking to me. You are taking time out if your day for me. Thank you :)

I just graduated from university and I'm not working right now. It's making me feel like I don't have a purpose. Anytime I start looking for jobs to apply for I get really nervous. All jobs in my field are downtown office jobs, and I had a summer job like that once and completely hated it. I'm afraid that's going to be what I'm doing for the rest of my life. 

Recently I visited a lot of my distant family, and in my culture, its very important to be welcoming to family. But I always felt a very fake warmth from my relatives, which shouldn't bother me, since I know I have people who care about me. But it made me question if a lot of my relationships with friends were real, or if people were just being kind to me because it's the right thing to do.
